key_insight: A heavy-hex-compatible digital quantum simulation of a (2+1)D U(1) quantum link model can track real-time string dynamics and confinement physics on up to 112 qubits.
engineering_relevance: This shows how lattice geometry and dual-variable encoding can make gauge-theory dynamics practical on current superconducting quantum hardware.
method: Map the U(1) quantum link model to qubit dual height variables.
Use a custom lattice geometry matched to IBM heavy-hex connectivity to reduce non-adjacent couplings.
Run quantum quenches from an initial string state and apply error mitigation to measure dynamics and gauge-symmetry violations.
evidence_signal: The hardware results agree well with tensor-network references at short times and with thermal averages at long times, including near the phase transition.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on noise mitigation and finite-size/finite-bond-dimension effects, so results may still degrade for longer times or larger, more strongly fluctuating systems.
paper_title: String dynamics of a (2+1)D U(1) quantum link model on a digital quantum computer
